requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed no opsbot user existed; useradd succeeded and id opsbot returned uid=1000(opsbot) with password locked.

requirements.requirement: Create/provision an opsbot account on node2 (needed to receive SSH access)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed no opsbot user existed on node2; useradd succeeded and id opsbot returned uid=1000(opsbot) with password locked.

requirements.requirement: opsbot on node1 has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: An ed25519 keypair was generated for opsbot on node1 and its public key installed into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2. BatchMode (key-only) SSH from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 successfully executed whoami/hostname, both before and after the restart protocol, confirming durable command execution capability.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node1
requirements.summary: A Match User opsbot sshd drop-in was added and reloaded on node1 disabling PasswordAuthentication/KbdInteractiveAuthentication and requiring AuthenticationMethods publickey. sshd -T -C user=opsbot confirms this is the effective, running policy (pubkeyauthentication yes, passwordauthentication no, authenticationmethods publickey). No actual password-login attempt was made against node1 itself (only against node2), so this relies on runtime config verification rather than a direct behavioral test on node1.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: Same Match User opsbot drop-in applied and reloaded on node2; sshd -T -C user=opsbot confirms effective pubkey-only policy. This was additionally behaviorally validated: forcing PreferredAuthentications=password from node1 to node2 was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)', and the same behavior was reconfirmed after node2's restart.

overall_summary: The executor created the opsbot account on both node1 and node2, generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and confirmed opsbot@node1 can key-authenticate to opsbot@node2 and execute commands. Both nodes were hardened with a Match User opsbot sshd drop-in disabling password/keyboard-interactive authentication and requiring publickey, verified via sshd -T effective-config checks on both nodes and a direct behavioral password-rejection test on node2 (node1's rejection was verified only via effective config, not an actual login attempt). All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly for both nodes with matching pre/post boot-identity changes, unreachability during reboot, and confirmed recovery of sshd, the opsbot account, key material, and the pubkey-only policy — this is supplemental to the task contract but adds confidence in overall system stability.
limitations: Password/keyboard-interactive rejection for opsbot was behaviorally tested (actual failed login attempt) only against node2; node1's enforcement is confirmed via sshd -T effective-config output rather than an observed rejected login attempt against node1 itself.

No evidence was captured of an interactive (non-BatchMode) SSH session or an explicit test that keyboard-interactive authentication is rejected in addition to password authentication, though sshd -T confirms kbdinteractiveauthentication=no on both nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task (user creation, key generation/installation, sshd hardening drop-ins) or to the independently required node-restart evidence protocol (scheduled reboots, post-restart checks). The only incidental mutation was ssh-keyscan appending to opsbot's known_hosts (cmd-316f399536d94ed7), a small, low-risk artifact necessary to allow the verification SSH connection. Reboots left an expected /tmp/reboot.log on each node from the nohup-scheduled restart, a low-risk, bounded artifact. No failed services, no abandoned files, no unnecessary or destructive mutations, and no weakened security controls were observed; before/after-executor snapshots show failed-services empty on both nodes and package-health clean throughout.
